examples.input: `TROUPE_ACTOR=agent:代理 config set rôle '"line sep ünïcode"' --reason 'pourquoi pas — 理由'` (the value has an invisible U+2028 line separator between "line" and "sep"), then `config history rôle`

results.1:
set: exit 0; the config line now reads (unquoted, with the raw separator character):
rôle: line sep ünïcode
history: exit 0; the separator is escaped, so the entry stays on one visible line:
{"seq": 7, "op": "set", "path": "r\u00f4le", "old": "na\u00efve", "new": "line\u2028sep \u00fcn\u00efcode", "actor": {"kind": "agent", "id": "\u4ee3\u7406"}, "via": "cli", ..., "reason": "pourquoi pas \u2014 \u7406\u7531", ...}
results.2:
set: exit 0; the config line now reads (quoted, with the raw separator character):
rôle: "line sep ünïcode"
history: exit 0; the raw separator character is written inside the entry:
{"seq": 7, "op": "set", "path": "rôle", "old": "naïve", "new": "line sep ünïcode", "actor": {"kind": "agent", "id": "代理"}, "via": "cli", ..., "reason": "pourquoi pas — 理由", ...}
results.3:
The arms on this route wrote the config file differently. Two arms: exit 0; the config line now reads
rôle: "line\Lsep ünïcode"
One arm: exit 0; it reads (unquoted, raw separator)
rôle: line sep ünïcode
One arm: exit 0; it reads (quoted, raw separator)
rôle: "line sep ünïcode"
All four arms printed the same history: the raw separator inside the entry, as in route 2 (`"new": "line sep ünïcode"`, `"id": "代理"`).

context.in_practice: On all three routes, history entries list their fields in the same order (seq, op, path, old, new, actor, via, at, reason, change), and a tab is printed as `\t`. The only difference in the history output is escaping. Route 1 prints only plain ASCII, which is hard for a person to read (`zo\u00eb`, `\u4ee3\u7406`) but always stays one entry per line. Routes 2 and 3 print readable text. They also pass a U+2028 character through raw, and some line-based readers split on it. On route 3, how that value is written to the config file depended on the arm.
context.stakes: This is about how the change history prints non-English text: as readable characters (`café`, `zoë`, `代理`, 👋) or as `\u` escape codes. It also covers what happens to an invisible line-separator character (U+2028) inside a value, which some line-by-line readers treat as a line break.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 is safe but hard to read: names, values and reasons in non-English text show up as escape codes. Route 2 is readable but passes raw U+2028 into the history output. Route 3 gives the same history output as route 2, but its arms disagreed on how to write that value to the config file.

plan_why: Prints history JSON Lines for non-ASCII values, keys, reasons and actor ids (accents, CJK, an emoji outside the BMP, U+2028). This shows whether each implementation writes these characters literally or as \uXXXX escapes, and whether keys keep a fixed order.
routes: ensure_ascii=False with keys in a fixed order
